problem_motivation.content: There is a lack of research and analysis on the high-temperature oxidation resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys, which limits their application despite their excellent mechanical properties at high temperatures.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Previous studies focused on mechanical properties at high- and room-temperatures, but with little research and analysis on high-temperature oxidation resistance [ [7] , [8] , [9] ].

problem_motivation.content: Adding oxidation-resistant elements like Al, Cr, and Si creates a trade-off by forming brittle intermetallic compounds that reduce mechanical properties.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Unfortunately, elements Al, Cr, and Si very easily form brittle intermetallic compounds with other refractory elements, resulting in reduced mechanical properties of RHEAs [ [14] , [15] , [16] ].

problem_motivation.content: W-based binary alloys suffer from performance shortcomings in heat insulation and radiation protection applications.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The successful preparation of WVTaTiCr alloy coating compensates for the performance shortcomings of some W-based binary alloys

prior_approach.content: Laser cladding is used to prepare WVTaTiCr x refractory high-entropy alloy coatings on 42-CrMo steel plate.
prior_approach.evidence_span: refractory high-entropy alloy coatings were prepared on a 42-CrMo steel plate using laser cladding

prior_approach.content: Previous research has utilized W-based binary alloys such as W-Ta, W-V, W-Ti, and W-Cr for nuclear applications.
prior_approach.evidence_span: In recent years, W-based alloys have been widely used in the nuclear energy industry, and W-Ta [ [17] ], W-V [ [18] ], W-Ti [ [19] ], W-Cr [ [20] ] have been studied.

prior_limitation.content: W-based binary alloys exhibit brittle behavior and reduced ductility, hindering their use in harsh environments.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Research results showed that some W-based binary alloys showed brittle behavior [ [21] ]. The reduction in ductility makes it difficult for W-based binary alloys to be widely used in harsh working environments

prior_limitation.content: Conventional sintering and PVD approaches suffer from segregation, embrittlement, porosity, or thickness limitations.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: The high-entropy alloys undergo segregation when prepared by melting, and embrittlement and porosity are attributes of conventional sintering, whereas the low thickness of the final product is a limit of the physical vapor deposition (PVD) approach [ [28] ].

prior_limitation.content: Electrodeposition techniques result in defects such as pores and microcracks in the resulting coatings.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: In addition, electrodeposition techniques lead to pores and microcracks in the coating [ [29] ].

rejected_alternative.content: Conventional sintering was not used because it causes segregation, embrittlement, and porosity in high-entropy alloys.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: The high-entropy alloys undergo segregation when prepared by melting, and embrittlement and porosity are attributes of conventional sintering

rejected_alternative.content: Physical vapor deposition (PVD) was rejected because it cannot produce coatings with sufficient thickness.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: whereas the low thickness of the final product is a limit of the physical vapor deposition (PVD) approach [ [28] ].

rejected_alternative.content: Electrodeposition was avoided because it introduces pores and microcracks into the coating.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: In addition, electrodeposition techniques lead to pores and microcracks in the coating [ [29] ].

inspiration_source.content: The study draws upon the advantages of laser cladding technology, which forms firm bonds, has a small heat-affected zone, and allows for millimeter-level coating thickness.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: Compared with magnetron sputtering, PTA welding, and additive manufacturing, the research shows that the cladding layer forms firm metallurgical bonds with the substrate, the heat-affected zone of the coating is small, the deformation of the substrate is small, and the coating thickness can reach the millimeter level [ [30] ].

causal_claim.content: Increasing Cr content promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase.

causal_claim.content: Adding Cr significantly improves the hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance, and corrosion resistance of the coating.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The addition of Cr greatly improves the hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and corrosion resistance of the coating

causal_claim.content: The addition of Cr element results in a decrease in oxidation weight gain and oxidation rate.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The addition of Cr resulted in the smallest increase in oxidation weight of the Cr 1 RHEA coating

causal_claim.content: The addition of Cr promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase, which enhances hardness through precipitation strengthening.

mechanism_principle.content: Cr addition enhances lattice distortion, which slows atomic diffusion, thereby reducing the binding speed with oxygen and improving oxidation resistance.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: With the addition of Cr, the internal lattice distortion effect of the WVTaTiCr alloy is the strongest, and the diffusion rate of each atom is the slowest, resulting in a decrease in the binding speed with external oxygen elements

mechanism_principle.content: The formation of a dense oxide film (CrTaO4, TiO2, Cr2O3) inhibits oxygen atom diffusion, reducing the oxidation rate.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The dense oxide film inhibits the diffusion of oxygen atoms, reduces the oxidation rate, and improves oxidation resistance

mechanism_principle.content: Cr addition enhances solid-solution strengthening, which further increases hardness.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In addition, with the increase in Cr content, the solid-solution strengthening effect in the alloy is enhanced, which further increases the hardness

mechanism_principle.content: Cr promotes the formation of a denser, more uniform passive film by filling vacancies, which reduces ion diffusion and lowers corrosion rate.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The addition of Cr can promote the generation of the passive film on the surface of the alloy coating, while the oxide deposition of Cr can fill the vacancy of the passive film, making the surface passive film become denser and uniform, thus reducing the diffusion and penetration rate of ions in the NaCl solution
